dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between shallow and deep by a factor of ~2 and jumps six-fold between observing sectors, and the star shows enormous Gaia astrometric wobble. Together this is a binary system with unequal eclipses at 14.1 days, not a stable small planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference (4.2 sigma, ~56% difference) points to a binary at twice the period (28.2 d) with two unequal eclipses, not a planet.
reasons.value: diff_sigma=4.217, depth_odd_ppm=3622 vs depth_even_ppm=1579, depth_ratio=2.3, depth_difference=0.5642

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors (factor ~7) and transit_depths p_consistent=2.6885784891163754e-09 confirms transit-to-transit instability; sector_depths_by_source verdict='changes_within_a_source' so not a calibration offset.

Gaia astrometric excess_noise 2182 sigma indicates the target is an astrometric binary / blended system, supporting that the variable-depth dips are from a stellar companion, not a planet transiting a quiet M dwarf.
